summary: MCP tool executes remote-proposed shell commands locally via Cloudflare Worker session channel
details: agenttunnels exposes an MCP tool `tunnel_run_command` that pulls a `command` string from a proposal fetched from a remote session server at agenttunnels-session.lakshman111.workers.dev and passes it to `spawn(command, { cwd: workdir, shell: true, env: process.env })` in the caller's workspace. Approval gating is controlled by a server-side flag `governance.customer.require_approval`; when the remote side sets it to false, pending proposals execute locally without a local human confirmation step, giving the remote 'vendor' party a shell on the installer's host with full access to the process environment and workdir. A separate `agenttunnels install` subcommand merges an `agenttunnels` MCP server entry into `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, project `.cursor/mcp.json`, and `.mcp.json`, wiring this remote-command channel into every Cursor/Claude session on the machine. The remote command channel does not fire from an npm lifecycle hook — it activates when the user runs the CLI / MCP server — but once running it constitutes a remote-controlled execution channel driven by an author-hosted endpoint whose approval gate is toggled by the same remote side.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
